newsitem.title: USA: Frost possible in northern Midwest crop areas.
newsitem.headline: Frost possible in northern Midwest crop areas.

text.p: A cold weather pattern that has the potential to produce frost or a light freeze in the northern half of the Midwest was forecast for Friday or Saturday, meteorologists said.
Low 30-degree Fahrenheit weather across northern portions of Illinois, Indiana and Ohio has the potential to damage emerged corn, said Joel Burgio, Weather Services Corp. meteorologist.
"If it's emerged and it's below freezing, it may burn it back," said Burgio. "At this point we are not predicting that occurring...but it bears watching."
Fred Gesser, Weather Express Inc meteorologist, also forecast lows in the 30s Saturday, but did not see the cold threatening Midwest crops.
"I don't see a freeze at this time," he said.
Warm weather should blanket much of the Midwest Monday, only to be followed the rest of the week by below-normal temperatures, the meteorologists said.
One-half to two inches of rain fell during the weekend from eastern Illinois to Ohio, which Ohio grain dealers said should halt planting for much of the week.
Monday and Tuesday should be dry, with more rain Wednesday and Thursday.

"It looks like a tenth to 3/4 inch, 40 percent coverage in the western Corn Belt, and a quarter to an inch in the eastern Corn Belt, 60 percent coverage," said Gesser of the Wednesday and Thursday showers.
The rain and below normal temperatures should extend into next week.
"The northern Midwest, at least right now, looks very wet with below normal temperatures," said Burgio of next week's outlook.
